sources.claim: Certificate and clearance depend on the work/protocol and licensed professional involvement; owner/construction exemptions can affect what documentation is obtainable. Do not assume any cleanup invoice entitles owner to CMDR.

faq.a: It is a Certificate of Mold Damage Remediation. TDLR explains that the document addresses the mold contamination identified for the project and whether the underlying cause was corrected. Read the actual project details and professional certifications.

faq.q: Must a Texas seller give a buyer recent mold-remediation certificates?
faq.a: TDLR says a seller must provide the buyer copies of the certificates received for that property within the preceding five years. Ask your Texas real estate professional how to handle the records and other disclosure requirements in your transaction.

faq.q: Is a cleanup invoice the same as the certificate?
faq.a: No. A receipt can document billed work, but it does not by itself establish the findings or certifications of a CMDR. Ask the professionals involved which documents were issued and what they support.

faq.q: Does a cash as-is sale remove the certificate handoff?
faq.a: Do not assume that. An as-is proposal addresses the purchase and condition; it does not replace applicable record-delivery or disclosure duties. Discuss known history and missing records before closing.
